blocks.title: Epoch-guarded segment reclamation
blocks.statement: WHILE any active reader lease holds epoch <= segment.max_epoch, the compaction sweeper SHALL retain the read-only mmap region and MUST NOT unlink the backing segment.

scenarios.name: Pinned reader defers munmap()
scenarios.given: segment seg-000479 is retired at epoch 9104 and 4 readers hold epoch 9098
scenarios.when: the compaction sweeper scans retired segments
scenarios.then: seg-000479 remains mapped until all 4 readers advance >= 9104

scenarios.name: Expired reader lease triggers copy-on-expire
scenarios.given: a slow snapshot cursor exceeds the 30-second epoch lease
scenarios.then: unread frames materialize into a bounded private buffer and the segment unmaps cleanly

blocks.title: Slow reader cursor delays retired segment unlink

decisions.label: Approve per-shard warm standby pool & reader lease policy

questions.text: How many 64 MiB standby segments should each shard pre-allocate?

options.label: 1 segment (64 MiB)
options.summary: Minimal disk footprint, but back-to-back burst rollovers can still hit synchronous fallocate().

options.label: 2 segments (128 MiB)
options.summary: Absorbs double-rollover bursts with zero append stalls across all 8-writer benchmarks.

options.label: 4 segments (256 MiB)
options.summary: Over-reserves NVMe space on high-density multi-shard hosts without measurable p99 gain.

recommendation.text: Pre-allocate 2 segments (128 MiB) per shard to eliminate rollover stalls while keeping multi-shard NVMe reservation bounded.

questions.text: Which reader-epoch lease timeout should gate copy-on-expire reclamation?

options.label: 10-second lease
options.summary: Reclaims disk fastest, but risks copying long analytical scans prematurely.

options.label: 30-second lease
options.summary: Covers 99.98% of point-in-time reads without triggering copy-on-expire.

recommendation.text: Enforce a 30-second reader epoch lease so analytical scans complete zero-copy while bounding worst-case segment retention.

questions.text: Should cold snapshots remain uncompressed deterministic POSIX tar or add Zstandard framing?

options.label: Deterministic POSIX tar
options.summary: Zero external codec dependencies; byte-stream seekable at 1,840 MiB/s.

options.label: Zstandard-framed tar (level 3)
options.summary: 2.84x smaller storage footprint; requires pinned zstd decoder across all verifiers.

recommendation.text: Keep uncompressed deterministic POSIX tar until cold store volume exceeds 50 GiB.
